# ADR digest — one line per ADR

Full text: `genesis-ctx adr <ID>` (loads the amendment chain). Areas: `genesis-ctx area <name>`. Untagged = not yet routed (47-05).

- ADR-001 — LangGraph owns control flow; agents never orchestrate.
- ADR-002 — Run agent steps as narrow Kiro turns via `kiro-agent-sdk` over ACP, with per-node MCP injection; NO global Kiro `mcp.json`.
- ADR-003 — Genesis is a local web app (engine + Kiro/MCP run locally with the user's creds) pulling workflows from a shared GitLab library; users are internal Solutions staff.
- ADR-004 — Inject MCP servers per node (per agent turn); never rely on globally-installed agents or a global Kiro `mcp.json`.
- ADR-005 (amended by 029) — The shared MCP/CLI registry lives in the library (curated tier, changed via MR) — no per-user "profiles".
- ADR-006 — Each workflow is a self-contained folder package (`workflow.yaml` + `graph.py`) in the `registry.json` catalog; users install selectively, pinned by ref in a lockfile.
- ADR-007 — Roles are filter tags + curated bundles, never hard gating — users may pick workflows across roles.
- ADR-008 — One local app bundles engine + UI; LangGraph Studio was the interim harness, the custom workbench is the product UI.
- ADR-009 — All three HITL modes are REQUIRED: designed approval gates, ad-hoc pause/resume anywhere, and mid-run state injection.
- ADR-010 — Keep state small/serializable/editable (pointers + decisions); bulk lives in the `RunWorkspace` blackboard under `$GENESIS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`; never inline bulk in state/chat.
- ADR-011 — The reliability trio (validator + retry + escalation) is MANDATORY on every agent node; CI-enforced.
- ADR-012 — Run graph execution in a disposable subprocess worker, not the app (pause=kill, resume=fresh worker from checkpoint); the app never imports workflow Python.
- ADR-013 — solutions-copilot is retired: Genesis owns its own config UI (GitLab token, MCP secrets, environments), reusing only its concepts as fresh implementations.
- ADR-014 — Author workflows via the `create-workflow` scaffolder (reliability trio pre-wired), the local test harness and the library steering; contribution is open.
- ADR-015 — Build order: the complete app + ERD reference first, then the custom workbench, then migrate skills to workflows one by one.
- ADR-016 — Names: platform `genesis`, library `genesis-workflows`, SDK `kiro-agent-sdk`.
- ADR-017 — One language — Python — for engine, nodes and workflows (3.11+; ADR-024 pins 3.13).
- ADR-018 — Hand bulk data between nodes via the blackboard (pointers in state), never inline in state or chat.
- ADR-019 (amended by 080) — The loader refuses a library whose `genesis_core_major != CORE_MAJOR` (=1, independent of the shared pip version); changes within a major are additive-only.
- ADR-020 (amended by 029) — Never mutate the user's global Kiro configuration — NO global Kiro `mcp.json`; MCP servers are injected per node over ACP.
- ADR-021 (amended by 068,082) — `META.auto_approve=true` by default; pause only at approval|escalation|pre_mutation gates; `pre_mutation` REQUIRED before any write/deploy/data MCP node, unless a confirm is the approval (ADR-068, ADR-082).
- ADR-022 — Write run artifacts under the dedicated, configurable artifacts root (`$GENESIS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`) with retention; never inline bulk in state.
- ADR-023 — The backend is FastAPI EMBEDDING LangGraph (NOT a LangGraph Server); Studio is an interim debug harness only.
- ADR-024 — The engine is async-first (ainvoke/astream + `AsyncSqliteSaver` + aiosqlite); Python is pinned to 3.13.
- ADR-025 — "Fork" = seed a NEW thread from a past checkpoint; never time-travel in-thread — the original is untouched.
- ADR-026 (amended by 063,085) — Web UI = React+TS for a local single-user app; `genesis serve`/`up` refuse a non-loopback bind unless explicitly opted in (`--i-understand-no-auth`) — Genesis ships no auth.
- ADR-027 — Use the established web stack (Tailwind + shadcn/Radix + React Router + TanStack Query + React Flow + …); reuse existing primitives and design tokens, not raw palette colors.
- ADR-028 (amended by 085) — ALL backend endpoints live under `/api` (+ SPA history fallback; only static Playwright reports sit on their own loopback origin, ADR-085); the client prepends `/api` centrally — never in components.
- ADR-029 (amends 005,020; amended by 083) — Two-tier MCP/CLI registry: curated read-only (MR-governed) + custom user-writable; tool trust = `node.tools ∩ server.allowlist`, a cap only for a node with a tool list (ADR-083: without one it trusts every tool).
- ADR-030 (amended by 037,041) — Persistence stays SQLite; move to Postgres/pgvector only on an explicit trigger (multi-user, transcript RAG, heavy analytics); keep repository signatures DB-agnostic.
- ADR-031 (amended by 033,034,045,076) — Chat is read-only: it observes/answers, never orchestrates or mutates; trust is fail-closed (read-only `@server/tool` allowlist + `auto_deny`); writes only in the per-session sandbox (ADR-034).
- ADR-032 — Credit usage is REAL metered data from Kiro ACP (per turn), NEVER estimated — no pricing engine; every figure carries `provenance` (metered/partial/unavailable).
- ADR-033 (amends 031; amended by 034) — The chat copilot may operate runs only at the run-management layer: every mutation is human-confirmed, it NEVER auto-approves a workflow's HITL gate, and gets NO config/secret/registry/deploy tools.
- ADR-034 (amends 031,033) — Skills are first-class standalone activities beside Workflows, chat-invoked + filesystem-provisioned; chat writes ONLY inside the per-session skill-output sandbox (`fs_write_root`).
- ADR-035 — Run input files (`format:"file"`) are provisioned into the run blackboard at launch via the multipart upload, never passed inline; bounded and sanitized.
- ADR-036 (amended by 073) — Genesis owns the Appian KB: a Genesis-native parser + a local KB in `genesis.db`, fed only by the single dev-tagged environment (`is_dev`); Atlas/Jarvis are retired as KB sources.
- ADR-037 (amends 030; amended by 073) — The KB stores only metadata/structure/dependency graph/bundles — NEVER SAIL source; all code (current + historical) is fetched live via the Dev MCP.
- ADR-038 (amended by 073) — Run the Dev + DevOps MCP servers as managed, vendored, versioned local installs (replaceable, never forked), launched from the per-server venv.
- ADR-039 — Business understanding is an agent-synthesized, evidence-grounded artifact built by a deterministic workflow from the local code-free KB only.
- ADR-040 — Install the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) as a managed, versioned local binary resolved via the CLI registry (the CLI analog of ADR-038).
- ADR-041 (amends 030) — Documents are one global store (dedup by source id, latest version only) LINKED into applications; untracking an app removes its links, never the documents.
- ADR-042 (amended by 075) — Features & Specs are first-class sub-entities of an application (cascade with it); a spec is authored conversationally in Chat, not by a workflow, and HTML is authoritative.
- ADR-043 — Embed the vendored Lavish annotation SDK (MIT) for in-app HTML review, themed from design tokens — don't run its server.
- ADR-044 {amended} (amended by 056; superseded by 056) — A Feature is a workspace of artifact stages, each with its own status (no feature status derived from one artifact); the sequential unlock is superseded by ADR-056.
- ADR-045 (amends 031; amended by 076) — The reused chat mirrors the Kiro CLI/ACP surface (model selection, slash commands, compaction, image prompts) while staying within ADR-031's read-only posture.
- ADR-046 (amended by 080) — Genesis ships as a local, browser-based app: clone + venv + `scripts/install-packages.sh`, launched by `genesis up`, self-updated by git tag.
- ADR-047 (amended by 074,081) — Scheduled maintenance syncs are fixed and backend-defined; the app sync is re-runnable as a full-package refresh.
- ADR-048 — Core Appian-MCP credentials are environment-scoped: stored per environment in the SecretProvider (never in `environments.json`) and resolved ONLY from the dev-tagged env.
- ADR-049 (amended by 061) — Applications-first IA: primary nav is Applications · Chat · Runs · Documents, Applications is the landing; Overview + Catalog live in Settings.
- ADR-050 (amended by 076) — Model SDLC lifecycle state as typed domain objects; EVERY status change goes through the single `LifecycleService.transition` authority.
- ADR-051 — The workflow-agent turn path depends on the `AgentProvider` Protocol (`KiroAcpProvider` default), never binds nodes to the Kiro/ACP loader directly.
- ADR-052 — Source documents only through the `DocumentProvider` Protocol (provider-neutral `DocRef`/`DocMeta`).
- ADR-053 — The Agentic Memory Layer distills persistent memory from stored conversations in two scopes; personal memory is never shared.
- ADR-054 — Memory lives in a separate `~/.genesis/memory.db` with its own migrations (genesis.db untouched) and a local embedder.
- ADR-055 — Light-first, MUI-inspired design language by evolving the existing tokens + Tailwind + shadcn-style primitives — NOT adopting `@mui/material`.
- ADR-056 (amends 044; amended by 057,058,078) — A Feature is a workspace of parallel, independently-advanceable, plug-in stage containers over a shared substrate; each stage has its own lifecycle.
- ADR-057 (amends 056; amended by 058) — The UX Design stage turns an uploaded PDF mockup into a grounded UX Implementation Analysis via the deterministic `ux-design-analysis` workflow.
- ADR-058 (amends 056,057) — The Technical Design stage turns the finalized Spec + UX analysis into a grounded, workstream-decomposed, object-level design; a stage MAY declare prerequisites.
- ADR-059 (amended by 075) — The Feature Breakdown stage turns Spec + UX + Technical Design into a grounded, workstream-decomposed, Jira-ready backlog.
- ADR-060 (amended by 075) — Finalize Stories is a one-time, IRREVERSIBLE action on a completed Feature Breakdown that turns its backlog into first-class, editable Story records.
- ADR-061 (amends 049; amended by 062,084) — The Workbench is a curated set of per-application Kanban boards over finalized stories, with eight fixed lanes; board membership is explicit (v0.69.0 amendment).
- ADR-062 {amended} (amends 061; amended by 068; superseded by 068) — Dragging a ticket into Design opens a confirm dialog that launches the design workflow; ADR-068 supersedes its proposal-only clause for the Implementation lane.
- ADR-063 (amends 026; amended by 065,074) — Genesis stays local-first and single-user; collaboration is an OPT-IN, selective centralization of a defined data subset to the shared Hub.
- ADR-064 — The Hub is a dedicated `Genesis Hub` Appian app in the existing dev env, exposing a FROZEN Web API contract.
- ADR-065 (amends 063) — Collaboration is active only when BOTH gates are on: the env master `GENESIS_COLLAB_ENABLED` and the Settings switch (gated on Hub availability).
- ADR-066 — Capture what each agent was given and produced, per iteration, and expose it in the run-detail node summary + turn explorer.
- ADR-067 — Use genesis-core `attach_healing` (grounded verify → heal → patch in place or one guided restart → escalate, bounded by `META.healing`) as the second reliability tier beside the ADR-011 trio.
- ADR-068 (amends 021,062; amended by 082) — Implementation is the only lane that mutates design objects; its confirm is the single blanket approval (rollback doc first); NEVER delete an object, no delete* tool (ADR-082: test users write QA app data).
- ADR-069 — A workflow agent node declares Kiro skills via `kiro_node(skills=[...])`; Genesis provisions them into the blackboard's `.kiro/skills/` — never rely on the host's global `~/.kiro/skills`.
- ADR-070 — The Object Wiki is a local-first, Hub-shared, APPEND-ONLY per-object change ledger.
- ADR-071 — ONE canonical story page (`/applications/:appUuid/stories/:storyId`) reached from every entry point; no parallel story surfaces.
- ADR-072 — Every finalized or created story gets a global, monotonic `GNS_<6-digit>` id allocated from `kb_sequences` inside the finalize/create transaction.
- ADR-073 (amends 036,037,038) — Package tools are used ONLY by Genesis program code (`DevMcpPackages`), never by agents or chat, and only on `genesis-delta-*` packages — the only sanctioned non-design-object write.
- ADR-074 (amends 047,063) — KB sync is incremental and package-scoped: list objects modified since this machine's own last sync (`covered_until`) and parse only those.
- ADR-075 (amends 042,059,060) — Every spec section/clause carries a hidden `data-cid` that PROGRAM code owns and repairs; stories trace to spec clauses.
- ADR-076 (amends 031,045,050) — A locked spec changes only through a change request: chat drafts the CR, program code applies the plan.
- ADR-077 — Agents load L0 + role + a genesis-ctx task pack, never the bulk docs whole; rules are selected by program (tags/areas/paths), never by search; history is archived verbatim; never run with --trust-all-tools.
- ADR-078 (amends 056; amended by 081) — A fifth feature stage, Test Design, starts after stories are finalized; Finalize once into ordered TS- scenarios that reference reusable TC- cases; Draft → Ready → Retired, retire not delete.
- ADR-079 — Cases link to stories (fingerprinted → Needs review) and to KB-confirmed objects by (app_uuid, object_uuid); impact walks kb_dependencies inbound on demand (direct + N hops, default 2) and stores nothing.
- ADR-080 (amends 019,046) — The platform is one repo: the app at the root, genesis-core, kiro-agent-sdk and the parser under packages/; no internal package lists another as a dependency; one install command; one shared version = the tag.
- ADR-081 (amends 078,047) — Test code lives as files in a per-app git workspace and genesis.db holds only the catalog; scripts reference actions and cases, never copy them; executions are program-only and run committed code.
- ADR-082 (amends 068,021) — All test execution and agent browser sessions run only on the single QA environment, as the app's test users, changing application data through the UI only — never design objects, deployments or MCP writes.
- ADR-083 (amends 029) — Phase 51 browser agents use Kiro's shell with the workspace's own apwt on program-opened, QA-pinned sessions; credentials never reach the agent; the missing isolation is an accepted risk until Phase 52.
- ADR-084 (amends 061) — Deployment precedes Verification; dragging a story into Verification (after confirming QA has its changes) launches story-verification; pass → Done, product defect → Implementation, blocked → a gate.
- ADR-085 (amends 028,026) — Serve Playwright reports only from a second loopback origin (app port + 100): static report files, no /api, GET/HEAD only, Host-checked, no traversal — never from the app's own origin.
